transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because... for months now, I’ve been seeing the same pattern in my project files at work. Certain subcontractors and one colleague in particular keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. They're doing it so it looks like my quality control failed. And, you know, even when IT looks into it and says the audit trail is clean, I know what I'm looking at. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is around?
No, I haven't heard any voices. I mean, it's not like that. It's just the files... the physical evidence is right there on the screen. It's not in my head, it's in the data. So, no, no voices.
Have you had similar beliefs about people trying to interfere with or blame you in other parts of your life, outside of work?

No, not at all. Outside of this specific project issue... I mean, my life is pretty normal. I still do my regular translation work, I manage my team's workflow without any problems. At home, I pay the bills, keep up with all the usual family routines. 

It's really just... the only place things ever go off track is when that specific file history or those certain coworkers come up. Everywhere else, everything is fine. Nobody is interfering with me outside of that.
Have you generally been suspicious and mistrustful of other people for as long as you can remember?

No, not at all. I've never really been a suspicious person. I mean, I usually trust people just fine, and I always have. 

That's... I think that's why this whole situation at work is so frustrating for me. I'm not the type of guy who just assumes people are out to get him or has trust issues. I'm just reacting to what's actually happening with those specific files. But in general? No, I've never had a hard time trusting people.
If someone presented clear evidence that the file history had not been altered, would you be able to consider that you might be mistaken?

Well, the thing is... I actually have been shown what they call clear evidence. IT looked at the system and told me the audit trail is completely clean. But... I can't just say I might be mistaken, because I'm the one looking at the data every day. 

For months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files. It's certain subcontractors and one specific colleague—they keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. They do it specifically so it looks like my quality control failed. So, even when IT says the audit trail is clean and everything looks normal to them, I know what I'm seeing. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
Have you ever had any other long-standing beliefs that other people were watching, deceiving, or trying to harm you in different situations?

No, I haven't. Honestly, I've never experienced anything like that before. Nobody has ever watched me or tried to harm me in the past. 

It's really just... it's just this one specific issue with the project files and those particular coworkers. Before all this started at work, I never had any reason to think anyone was trying to deceive me in any way.
Do you think the changes to the files are happening through ordinary human actions at work, or do you believe something unusual or impossible is causing them?

No, it's nothing like that. I don't think it's anything impossible or... supernatural, if that's what you mean. 

It's just ordinary people doing ordinary things on a computer. They're just logging in, opening the files, and making edits to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's just normal software manipulation that anyone with the right access could do. There's nothing magical about it, it's just... it's just very deliberate, careful sabotage by the people I work with.
